channel.title: RadialDeck blog
channel.description: Practical guides for working faster in Windows.

item.title: Windows clipboard history: the 25-item limit and how to work with it
item.description: Win+V keeps your last 25 copies, up to 4 MB each, and forgets them when you restart. What it keeps, what it drops, how pinning works, and faster ways to paste the things you copy most.

item.title: Radial menu for Windows 11: what a pie menu is and how to set one up
item.description: A radial (pie) menu puts your commands in a circle around the cursor, so you pick one by direction instead of reading a list. Why that is faster, what Windows 11 offers, and how to add one in a few minutes.

item.title: Quick Launch in Windows 11: where it went and four alternatives
item.description: Windows 11 removed taskbar toolbars, and with them the old Quick Launch bar. What still works for opening programs fast, from taskbar pins and Win+number to a launcher ring under the cursor.

item.title: Outlook Quick Steps: useful examples, their limits, and a faster way to reply
item.description: Quick Steps bundle several Outlook actions into one click. Practical examples to set up today, what changes in the new Outlook, where Quick Steps stop, and how a ring under the cursor covers the rest.

item.title: Kando alternatives for Windows: three ways to get a pie menu
item.description: Kando is a good free pie menu. If you are on Windows and want something different, here is a fair comparison of Kando, RadialDeck and a pie menu you script yourself in AutoHotkey.

item.title: How to copy text from the screen in Windows 11
item.description: Text in a picture, a video, an error dialog or a PDF scan you cannot select? Windows 11 can read it for you. Four ways to copy text from anywhere on the screen, and when each one is the right tool.

item.title: Excel paste values shortcut, and what to do when it does not work
item.description: Every keyboard way to paste values only in Excel for Windows, why each one sometimes fails, and how to turn paste values into one flick of the mouse.

item.title: An AutoHotkey alternative with a GUI: shortcuts and macros without scripts
item.description: AutoHotkey can automate almost anything on Windows, but you have to write and maintain scripts. When that is worth it, when a tool you configure with clicks is easier, and how to move common AutoHotkey jobs into a radial menu.
